title: AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears 15GW threshold by H2 2026
body: By H2 2026 the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears a 15GW cumulative threshold, anchored by the third-consecutive-week sovereign-cloud signing cadence and the AI-accelerator IPO comparable set that Wednesday's tape has now firmed into a single readable supply-and-demand picture. The Wednesday catalysts trace a tightening run-up to the T-minus-one-day Thursday May 21 Alphabet analyst day. A Wednesday HPCwire AIwire note reports the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book advancing to near 10.7GW with a fresh weekday sovereign-cloud commitment, the third new commitment of the business week and the highest weekly cadence the book has carried since the program opened. A Wednesday Datacenter Dynamics wire reports the Tenstorrent Galaxy-rack first-half capacity-fulfillment curve crossing the 70-percent threshold for the first time, at roughly 71 percent of the 280-rack target on a cumulative count of 198 racks deployed, with the third European sovereign-cloud increment of the week going to Outscale France plus Atlante Cloud Italy and the third Asia-Pacific increment splitting between Yotta Labs India and CDS Japan. The capital-markets backdrop hardens on the same Wednesday tape: Cerebras CBRS holds the Friday $198.60 close as its reference anchor with the five-desk analyst spread carrying inside a roughly $185-to-$235 band, institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging to about 39 percent of float on the analyst-day eve, and a Wednesday 247 Wall St note reporting the Mag-7 preview cohort clearing the 90-percent threshold on Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability — the first time the cohort consensus has cleared that line — with the cohort treating Wednesday's pre-print Cerebras session as a coincident input. The Wednesday AIwire note further reports Tenstorrent's SEC Corp Fin first-round comment-letter response at its 13-business-day mark inside the staff-review interval with the second-round letter expected late Thursday or Friday, the early-August public-filing target holding, and SambaNova's bookrunner roster steady at six — giving equity analysts a fresh three-name AI-accelerator IPO comparable set against which the AMD commitment-book trajectory and the Tenstorrent capacity-fulfillment curve land as the two readable demand-side anchors. The structural force is that once the commitment-book cadence runs at three new sovereign-cloud signings per business week with a sub-10-week run-rate of roughly 0.25GW per signing, the Tenstorrent capacity-fulfillment curve crosses 70 percent five-and-a-half months before the public-filing target with the second-round Corp Fin comment letter inside its staff-review window, and the Mag-7 cohort clears 90-percent breakout-probability against a settled Corp Fin disclosure precedent — the capital-and-capacity supply-demand picture compresses to arithmetic that lands the commitment book through 15GW inside H2 2026, well ahead of the program's original end-of-year-2026 marker. The most likely landing is the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clearing 15GW cumulative cleanly inside H2 2026 — likely Q3 — with the sovereign-cloud cohort accounting for the marginal-signing share above 12GW, the Tenstorrent confidential S-1 going public in early August leaning on the now-71-percent capacity-fulfillment curve as the revenue-traction anchor, and the Mag-7 fiscal-Q3 AI Services breakouts pricing the AMD book as a demand-side comparable. Bear case is that one of the next three sovereign-cloud commitments slips its execution window or the Tenstorrent S-1 ships before the AMD book reaches 12GW, deferring the 15GW landing into early Q4 2026; absent that slip, H2 2026 lands the AMD commitment book through 15GW.

reasoning.because: AMD commitment book advances to 10.7GW Wednesday with a third sovereign-cloud signing this week.
reasoning.given: Tenstorrent capacity fulfillment crosses 70 percent; Mag-7 cohort clears 90-percent breakout line.
reasoning.so_that: The AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears a 15GW cumulative threshold ahead of year-end.
reasoning.landing: By H2 2026; likely Q3; sovereign-cloud cohort drives the marginal-signing share.
reasoning.plain_language: AMD's order book for AI servers is filling so fast it will easily clear 15GW of orders by late 2026.

summary: Wednesday's AMD note advances the Helios plus MI450 commitment book to near 10.7GW with a third weekday sovereign-cloud signing, Tenstorrent capacity fulfillment crosses 70 percent, and the Mag-7 cohort clears 90-percent breakout probability. By H2 2026 the commitment book clears 15GW.
